items.quote: which for width $u=\mu^d$ is $O(u^{\tau})$ per unit volume
items.note: The recursion splits into W role streams at every level, which needs a row field divisible by W^d (paper line 1483, Proposition power-interchange). The page omits this hypothesis; the paper reaches arbitrary widths and shapes only after padding rows (Lemma at line 1631). As stated, the recursion for width mu^d is claimed for any array.

items.quote: So $q$ divides no numerator or denominator of the finitely many matrices used.
items.note: Does not follow from the preceding sentence, which only requires q not to divide the denominators xi. The paper (Lemma matrix-shear, around line 1417) requires a fixed odd prime avoiding every denominator in the table of factorizations and the numerators of diagonal entries of the invertible factors; avoiding all numerators and denominators is only a sufficient example choice. The page also never says which finite collection of matrices is meant or why such a q exists, so the reader cannot see why q can be fixed independent of b.

items.quote: Take an input role $w$ and its route to output role $\rho(w)$, carrying sign $\varepsilon_w \in \{+1,-1\}$.
items.note: Gates combine several wires, so a single route with a sign is not defined for an arbitrary network. It holds only because the scalar network as a whole is a signed permutation of roles; the paper (lines 816-823) derives the route formula from the whole-network identity D_out S D_in^{-1}, which the page never states. The page does not say the scalar network is a signed role permutation.

items.quote: A field of $u=m^k$ bits therefore has $Q_k=O(u^\tau)$, and the interchange costs $O(Vu^\tau)$.
items.note: Missing hypotheses. The paper's Proposition power-interchange (lines 1476-1487) requires width exactly a power m^k and a row field before both chunks whose length is divisible by W^k. The recursion needs enough rows to split into W role streams at every level. The page omits the row condition. Arbitrary widths u need a separate lemma (Lemma chunk-swap, line 1632) with padding, not this recurrence.

items.quote: Along a side wire, a label containing $t_T$ may grow to $t_S^\perp$, since $t_T\perp t_S$, adding $h-2$ dimensions.
items.note: Labels are subspaces of F=(Q^h)^{tensor 3}, but t_S^perp lies in Q^h and t_T is not a label of F; the paper (lines 945-955, 1048-1055) applies this only to the P tensor factor (P x <t_X> inside P x t_Y^perp), with other factors suppressed. The page gives no assignment of labels to the gates, so the reader cannot see how this relates to the labels U_iota.

items.quote: So the shear needs $\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Q}M$ interchanges plus $O(V)$ further work.
items.note: The paper's Lemma matrix-shear (line 1394) assumes every H field comes before every D field in tape order, which is what makes D_tau <- D_tau + H_sigma an update of a later field by an earlier one, doable in linear time. The page omits this layout hypothesis and the O(V) bound for the two additions is not justified without it.
